Letter from Jared Fiore dated August 14, 2026 RE: 193 Hartford Turnpike Page 2 of 2 Blaise P. Berthiaume Damien D. Berthiaume Padgett D. Berthiaume Ralph Igoe (1900-19620) Arthur L. Beaudette (1920-1982) August 6, 2026 Shrewsbury Planning Board 100 Maple Ave. Shrewsbury, MA 01545 & Via email to: planning@shrewsburyma.gov cmcgoldrick@shrewsburyma.gov RE: Spagtacular LLC 335 Maple Avenue, Shrewsbury Dear Planning Board Members: I am unable to attend tonight’s scheduled meeting on behalf of my client, Angela Ciamarra Mancini who is the owner of property located at 110 Oak Street, Shrewsbury so I am providing this correspondence to reiterate my client’s concerns and objections with respect to the proposal concerning 335 Maple Avenue, Shrewsbury (“the Project”). To my knowledge, the only revision to the plan since the last meeting appears to be a hand drawn plan depicting a driveway running from building 5 to the upper buildings. It is unclear from that plan how the accessible sidewalks that the Applicant has previously proposed would be impacted by this change. It does not appear from my review of this revision, that the Applicant has included the screening requested on behalf of my client. My client’s concerns with respect to this Project remain the same as those articulated in my letter of July 9, 2026. It appears that the Project as proposed continues to lack the integration between the uses that is definitionally required by the Shrewsbury Zoning By-Law. My client continues to suggest that the Applicant has failed to provide evidence to support the special permit criteria to justify allowing excess height for the residential buildings and suggests instead if the Board were to approve this Project, it should deny the requested Special Permit to construct 4 story buildings and limit the approval of the site to three-story residential buildings only, which is in accordance with the By-Law. While the applicant has identified cross-sections of the grades and buildings in terms of the impact on my client’s view, those cross sections have failed to identify the HVAC and associated equipment which we believe was discussed at prior meetings as being located on the roofs of the buildings. This calls into question, the overall height of 4 Elm Street, Post Office Box 190, North Brookfield, MA 01535 T: 508-867-6885 F: 508-867-3138 the buildings, including utility infrastructure as proposed, which the Board should carefully consider based upon specific and definitive height information to be provided by the Applicant. Finally, my client respectfully requests that if the Board were inclined to approve the Project, the Board should condition approval upon the inclusion of a significant buffer along all of the boundaries between the proposed Project and the existing residences on Oak Street as outlined in my letter of July 9, 2026. This request is increasingly important as the Applicant chose, this week, to cut an approximate 4’ swath along the boundaries of the Oak Street residences, thereby eliminating a section of the naturally existing buffer. The Board should consider this action and exercise its discretion to require a significant evergreen buffer zone along all of the Oak Street residential property boundaries, including without limitation, along the entire Access Road as a condition to approval. As presently designed, it appears that cars making a left from Oak Street into the Access Road will be shining headlights into my client’s residence and a significant buffer in that area in particular will provide a benefit to my client. Thank you for your consideration. Very truly yours, DDB/dd Damien D. Berthiaume db@berthiaumelegal.com 4 Elm Street, Post Office Box 190, North Brookfield, MA 01535 T: 508-867-6885 F: 508-867-3138 Jared A. Fiore Direct telephone: 508-318-1741 Email: jfiore@princelobel.com BY FIRST CLASS MAIL AND BY ELECTRONIC MAIL August 14, 2026 Planning Board C/O Julie Holstrom, Chairperson Town of Shrewsbury 100 Maple Avenue Shrewsbury, MA 01545 planning@shrewsburyma.gov Re: 193 Hartford Turnpike, Shrewsbury, MA Dear Members of the Planning Board: Reference is made to that certain meeting of the Town of Shrewsbury Planning Board, held on Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 7:00 PM (the “Meeting”). As you know, Yatco Energy, LLC has sought to develop a commercial property located on the Town of Shrewsbury, Massachusetts’s Assessor’s Tax Plate 52, Plot 000125, commonly known as 193 Hartford Turnpike, Shrewsbury, Massachusetts 01545 (the “Property”); As you also know, this Firm represents Demoulas Super Markets, Inc. (“DSM”) with respect to the Project and has challenged the legality of the Town of Shrewsbury Zoning Board of Appeals’ decision of October 3, 2024 and the Town of Shrewsbury Planning Board’s decision of September 12, 2025, including by filing Civil Action Nos. 2485CV01275 and 2685CV00078 in the Superior Court division of the trial court of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Worcester County (the “Civil Actions”). I have reviewed the video recording of the Meeting and was surprised to hear Mr. McGolderick’s statements that (1) he believed that the Civil Actions had been settled; (2) there has been site work performed; and (3) that there was a pre-construction meeting last week. Although DSM is hopeful that a resolution can be obtained, and the parties have been working in good faith, no such resolution has been achieved at this time. As such, the Civil Actions have not been settled and they remain pending in the Superior Court. I respectfully request that the Planning Board refrain from taking further action on issuing any Prince Lobel Tye LLP One MercanƟle Street Suite 220 Worcester, MA 01608 www.princelobel.com #6385034v1 permissions concerning the Project while the Civil Actions are pending. Thank you. Very truly yours, Jared A. Fiore JAF/pb cc: Christopher McGoldrick (via email only - cmcgoldrick@shrewsburyma.gov) Mark L. Donahue, Esq. title: Planning Board Public Hearing - Zoning Bylaw Amendments - Agricultural Uses
text: DIANE SUPCZAK-MULVANEY, Chair BOB SZKLARZ, Vice-Chair BRAD HUTCHISON Clerk LINDA GOUIN, Member VACANT, Member JOHN MULLIN, Associate Member Anne Capra, Director of Planning & Conservation acapra@southhadleyma.gov TOWN OF SOUTH HADLEY PLANNING BOARD NOTICE OF HYBRID PUBLIC HEARING Proposed Amendments to the Zoning Bylaw Regarding Agricultural Uses The South Hadley Planning Board will hold a hybrid public hearing on Monday, September 14, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. to discuss proposing articles to Town Meeting for the purpose of amending the Zoning Bylaw to repeal and replace § 255-25 “Agricultural, Horticultural and Floricultural Uses” with “Agricultural Uses Accessory to Residential Use”; repeal and replace § 255-26 “Stables and Riding Academies” with “Commercial Agricultural Uses”; amend § 255-10 to insert new definitions related to agricultural and related uses; amend § 255-24 regarding Accessory Uses and Buildings; amend § 255-41 regarding Outdoor Recreation Facilities; and amend the Zoning Use Schedule as relevant. These amendments seek to address inconsistencies within the Zoning Bylaw and ensure compliance with agricultural use protections identified under MGL Chapter 40A, Section 3; along with other relevant amendments. The public hearing will be held through hybrid format with in-person attendance to be located in the multipurpose room of the South Hadley Senior Center, 45 Dayton Street South Hadley MA 01075. Virtual attendance will be hosted through the log-in information below: URL to join: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89989664296?pwd=Fi6hkHiSrTiqQ4facFj9ZJ9bSJsbjS.1 Or join by phone: +1 (309) 205 3325 Webinar ID: 899 8966 4296 Passcode: 281320 The current drafts of the proposed bylaws and any accompanying documentation can be found here: https://www.southhadley.org/1318/ProposedDraft-Bylaws. Alternatively, hardcopies of the documents can be viewed at the Planning & Conservation Department Office (Room U6) in Town Hall. Any person interested in, or wishing to be heard, should appear/join the hearing at the time and in the manner designated. title: Select Board Agenda
text: AGENDA SELECT BOARD September 22, 2026 7:00 p.m. Town Building WORK SESSION o Setting expectations of the work session o Review Select Board Policies o Review Comprehensive Pian Short and Long Term Goals Posted Thursday, 9/17/2026 Setting expectations of the work session Review Select Board Policies Review Comprehensive Plan Short and Long Term Goals SHARED SB/TA GOALS BASED ON THE COMP PLAN STRATEGIES TIME FRAME On an ongoing basis, evaluate non-essential or unused Town-owned praperties to determine their potential best uses, and suggest disposition for housing, open space, additional municipal uses, leasing, or sale. Short Term Engage with MART, the MBTA, and the Boston Region MPO to improve regional transit services for Stow residents and workers. Short Term Continue to pursue renovation of the Old Town Hall for use as a multipurpose community space. Short Term Create a plan to identify what emergency and resilience needs could be met through facilities or programming upgrades or optimization at the Pompositticut Community Center. Short Term Coordinate with Maynard and the MWRA tc evaluate potential expansions of regional water and sewer infrastructure into Stow. Incorporate the findings of the forthcoming Public Water Feasibility Study, prioritize Lower Village and other key development areas, and seek opportunities for public-private partnerships. Long Term Develop an impact Assessment Toolkit to help Town boards, committees, commissions, and the public evaluate the impact of major proposals on the Town’s fiscal sustainability and obligations to community equity. This toolkit will provide a structured approach to forecasting the costs and benefits of development, including impacts on municipal services, tax rates, local education contributions, infrastructure needs, and community equity, ensuring fair and inclusive growth. This toolkit should Incorporate a publicly accessible online component with case studies, best practices, and examples from other communities to support informed decision-making and transparent discussions about the Town’s future growth. Long Term Reconvene an exploratory committee to make recommendations for ongoing community engagement strategies that build upon the work completed during the comprehensive plan process. Long Term Clarify roles and responsibilities regarding staff and Board/Committee involvement with construction of multi-modal transportation projects. Long Term Expand efforts on Town-owned properties that encourage native and climate-resilience plantings, pollinator pathways, and invasive species removal. Support ongoing public awareness efforts around best practices that support biodiversity and native wildlife. Long Term

This is an in-person meeting. Virtual attendance via Teams is offered as a convenience for our residents, but if technical issues prevent Teams from operating, the meeting will continue as planned. Remote access to the meeting can be obtained via the information below. For access questions, please reach out to Christa McGaha at cmcgaha@swampsottma.gov Click here to join the meeting Link to join: https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/220599306744943?p=VhERQTiOSrTnhlxmkV Meeting ID: 220 599 306 744 943 Passcode: cG99ib7k Join by Phone: +1 (323) 694-9686 Enter conference ID: 742 948 731# AGENDA 1. Approval of past meeting minutes 2. Public Hearing - 26-11 45 Pleasant Street by Kenneth B. Shutzer, Esq. c/o Michael Snitkovsky Requesting a Site Plan Special Permit to demolish the existing two-family dwelling and construct a five-unit condominium development, with each unit containing approximately 1,850 square feet of living area, together with associated parking and site improvements, in the A-4 Zoning District. Property address: 45 Pleasant Street (Map 23, lot 4) 3. Gainsboro Treasurer and Receiver General Chairman THE ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES CONTROL COMMISSION (“ABCC”) ADVISORY Effective July 1, 2010, the legislature passed a new law authorizing Local Liquor Licensing Authorities (“LLA”) to allow M.G.L. c. 138, §12 licensees to sell alcoholic beverages at 10 a.m. on Sundays. This law amends M.G.L. c 138, §33B by allowing each city or town to “opt into” the new law giving their LLA discretion to grant an additional one (1) hour of sale of alcoholic beverages on Sundays, now starting at 10 a.m. to any or all of the §12 licensee in their community. Cities and towns should check with their counsel to determine the procedure required to “opt into” this new law. ABCC approval for these discretionary hours of sale is not required; but as always the LLA must forward an informational “Form 43” with the Sunday hours of sale to the ABCC. Each §12 licensee should consult with their LLA to determine the necessary steps to get permission to sell alcoholic beverages at 10 a.m. on Sundays. A §12 license holder who is denied the discretionary hour of sale may not appeal that denial to the ABCC. All licensees should ensure that they are in compliance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, M.G.L. c. 138, §64, and that sales of alcoholic beverages take place only on the days and hours last approved by the LLA. NO §12 LICENSEE HAS THE RIGHT TO SELL ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES EXCEPT DURING THE HOURS the LLA PREVIOUSLY GRANTED ON OR BEFORE JUNE 30, 2010. ANY LICENSEE WHO SELLS BEFORE THE HOURS OF SALE PREVIOUSLY GRANTED ON OR BEFORE JUNE 30, 2010 BY THE LLA VIOLATES THE LAW AND FACES DISCIPLINARY ACTION FROM THE LLA BY SUSPENSION, REVOCATION, CANCELLATION OR MODIFICATION OF THE LICENSE IN ADDITION TO ARREST AND CRIMINAL PROSECUTION FOR THE ILLEGAL SALE OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES, Individuals with questions concerning this Advisory and the new Sunday Sales law may contact, the ABCC at 617-727-3040 x 31. (Issued: Friday, July 02, 2010)

title: Conservation Commission 9/24/2026 Meeting Agenda
text: Waltham Conservation Commission September 24, 2026 7:00 p.m. Meeting Agenda Pursuant to the relevant legislation, including Mass. Acts 2025 c.2, this meeting will take place remotely. All Open Meeting Law requirements will be met and public access will be available by Zoom call. Residents who need a device to connect are invited to use a public desktop or borrow a laptop at the Waltham public library (valid library card required). For this meeting, members of the public may participate by joining at: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/87919579472?pwd=3SaRyDI7lE3yDicahosv5iZhbU9zTT.1 Passcode: Waltham We will post a link to the video recording at http://www.wcac.org/government/meetings/conservationcommission as soon as possible after the meeting. Public Meeting Request for Determination of Applicability (continued from 9-10-2026) Applicant: Devin McArthur Property Location: 231 Second Ave Project Description: Reclaim, grade, pave, and stripe 37,370 sq.ft. commercial parking lot. No change to the current parking lot dimensions, only reestablishing a solid gravel base and repaving. Public Hearing Notice of Intent (DEP File # 316-tba) Applicant: George Sarris Property Location: 234 Calvary Street Project Description: Raze an existing commercial building and a garage and construct a new commercial building within the same building footprint. The entire lot is within the 100-year floodplain and 200’ Riverfront area. Commission Business • Approval of meeting minutes from 9-10-2026. Correspondence • INFORMATIONAL: MA DEP reminds all ConComs that drought status determinations are “backwards looking.” The Northeast Region (including Waltham) remains in drought and ConComs should not accept intermittent stream determinations made since 8/1/25 without additional investigation. Old Business • Site Visit Reports • Committee Reports • Paine Estate Forest Management Plan subcommittee. • CPC: Meeting scheduled for September 22. New Business •

title: Waltham City Council Meeting Docket
text: City Council Docket September 28, 2026 The Waltham City Council will meet in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 610 Main Street, Waltham, MA, on Monday, September 28, 2026, at 7:30 p.m. The following matters and others may be considered. Approval of Minutes Regular Meeting of September 14, 2026 Notice is hereby given that the City Council and the Board of Survey and Planning will hold a Joint Public Hearing in the City Council Chamber, City Hall, 610 Main Street, Waltham, Massachusetts, on Monday, September 28, 2026, at 7:30 P.M. on the following petition for a Zoning District Map Amendment. Public Hearing Zoning Ordinance Amendment at 181 – 185 Felton Street Union Avenue LLC, of 251 High Street #3, Waltham, Massachusetts 02453, as Petitioner; and 181 Felton Street Realty Trust, of 251 High Street #3, Waltham, Massachusetts 02453, as the Owner of the parcel of land known and numbered as 181 - 185 Felton Street (“Locus”), shown in the “Atlas City of Waltham, Massachusetts” as follows: ● Page 59, Block 30, Lot 22 181-185 Felton Street which land is the subject of the following Zoning District Map Amendment, pursuant to G.L. c. 40A, § 5, hereby petition the City Council of the City of Waltham to amend Part III (formerly Chapter 21) of the General Ordinances of the City of Waltham entitled "Zoning Code", and in particular to amend the “Zoning District Map” as follows: ARTICLE III entitled “Establishment of Districts”, Section 3.13 entitled "Zoning District Map" is hereby amended by expanding the Riverfront Overlay Zoning District over a portion of the locus, containing 18, 567 square feet, located in the Residence C Zoning District. Said portion of the locus being shown as “RESIDENCE C AREA TO BE ADDED TO THE RIVERFRONT OVERLAY ZONING DISTRICT = 18,567 SQ.FT.” on a plan entitled “Existing Zoning District Plan” within a set of plans entitled “Waltham City Council Plan to Accompany Petition For Zoning Map Change, Riverfront Overlay to Be Added to Residence C area, 181-185 Felton Street, Waltham, Massachusetts” dated January 7, 2026, revised March 24, 2026, and consisting of 4 sheets including the Cover Sheet, more particularly described in materials filed with this Petition. Or otherwise act thereon. Public Hearing 17-25 Street Opening at 205 Second Avenue Nationalgrid hereby petitions the City Council for the necessary authorization to request permission to cut a 5 x 4 opening at 205 Second Ave, Waltham. The street is under moratorium. Replacing gas main feeding building in the rear of 205 Second Ave. Driveway is privately owned. All work will be completed subject to Section 17-25 of the General Ordinances of the City of Waltham. The locus is known and numbered as 20 Williams Street and is shown in the “Atlas, City of Waltham, Massachusetts 1988”, as Map 59 Block 35 Lot 24. Kaitz, Trustee of the Sam-EJ Realty Trust, under Declaration of Trust dated March 26, 1993 and recorded with the Middlesex South Registry of Deeds in Book 23034, Page 602, P.O. Box 541421, Waltham, MA 02454. Public Hearing Fuel Storage License 40-50 & 60 Sylvan Road ARE-MA Region No. 82, LLC, 400 Technology Square, Suite 1000, Cambridge, MA 02139, has applied to the City of Waltham to amend existing Fuel Storage License No. 91 for the property located at 40-50 & 60 Sylvan Road, Waltham, Massachusetts. JOP EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR OF GENERAL GOVERNMENT SERVICES The Select Board will be meeting on Wednesday, September 22nd at 4:00 pm in the Juliani Room at Town Hall. We have moved upstairs given the public comment component of the meeting. 1. 2. 3. 4. 4:00 4:01 4:05 4:10 Call to Order – Open Session Citizen Speak Executive Director’s Update Consent Agenda Please find materials regarding the consent agenda item. Requests for removal from the consent agenda should be sent to the Executive Director or Chair by Monday morning. Should items not be removed from the Consent Agenda, here is a motion for acceptance: MOTION MOVE to approve the Consent Agenda. • Vote Cultural Council Appointment The Board is being asked to reappoint Tanya Auger to the Wellesley Cultural Council. Ms. Auger recently completed her first term on the Council and has submitted a volunteer application seeking a second term. Cultural Council Chair Marc Zawel has submitted a letter supporting the reappointment, citing Ms. Auger's participation in the Council's grant review process, her understanding of Wellesley's community organizations, and her experience in education, literature and arts programming. MOVE to appoint Tanya Auger to the Wellesley Cultural Council for a term to expire on June 30, 2029. • Vote Funds for Seasonal Wreaths The Town received a quote from Volante Farms for 176 seasonal wreaths in the amount of $4,924.48. For the past several years, the Select Board has funded the seasonal wreath’s and the request would be for the Board to fund this year as well. MOVE to approve the funds for the seasonal wreaths. • Vote One Day Licenses (2) for Wellesley Historical Society The Wellesley Historical Society has submitted applications for two one-day alcohol licenses for events at the Wellesley History & Exhibit Center, 323 Washington Street. Staff has reviewed both applications and recommends approval. The first is for the Society's Oktoberfest fundraiser, scheduled for October 29 from 6:00–8:30 p.m. (the date has shifted from their original submittal of October 8th) The 21+ event is expected to have approximately 75 attendees and will feature craft beer and food. The application seeks a wine and malt beverages license and includes the event layout, insurance documentation and responsible alcohol-server training information. The second is for the Society's annual Holiday Cocktail Party, scheduled for December 9 from 6:00–8:30 p.m. The event is also limited to approximately 75 attendees and will include wine, beer and appetizers. Proceeds from both events support the Historical Society's work preserving and promoting Wellesley's history. The application materials include the required event plan, insurance and alcohol-server training documentation. These are the 4th and 5th requests from the Historical Society in 2026. Groups are allowed 30 One Day licenses in any calendar year. MOVE to approve two one day licenses for the Wellesley Historical Society. 2026 State Election Warrant • Vote Warrant for 2026 State Election Please find the November 2026 State Election Warrant as prepared by the Town Clerk. Approval of the Warrant is part of the Town's required preparation for the election and provides formal notice to Wellesley voters of the election. The statewide election will be held Tuesday, November 3; early voting runs October 17–30. MOVE to approve the 2026 State Election Warrant • Vote Local Government Representative for Clean Energy Siting and Permitting Please find a memo Corey Testa and Marybeth Martello regarding the establishment of a Local Government Representative for Clean Energy Siting and Permitting – this is a consolidated permitting process – along with a slide show from DOER detailing the process. The NRC will be discussing Brandon’s appointment at their meeting on Tuesday, September 22nd. Beginning October 1, 2026, new state regulations under 225 CMR 29.00 require municipalities to offer an optional consolidated permitting process for certain small- and medium-scale clean energy projects, including qualifying solar, battery storage, and transmission/distribution projects. The process does not replace existing Town bylaws or the permitting authority of individual boards and departments; rather, it establishes a coordinated process with a single final decision and defined timelines. The regulations designate the Select Board as the default Local Government Representative (LGR) but allow the Board to appoint another municipal official. The LGR is primarily responsible for coordinating the process, determining application completeness, ensuring the appropriate boards and departments conduct their reviews, issuing the consolidated decision, and addressing site suitability and mitigation requirements. DOER identifies municipal planning, building, zoning and conservation officials as potential designees. CAC Director and Asst. Executive Director are recommending that the Board appoint NRC Director Brandon Schmitt as Wellesley's LGR effective October 1. His existing responsibilities for environmental and natural resource matters, regulatory experience, and coordination with multiple Town departments and boards are well aligned with the role. MOVE to appoint NRC Director Brandon Schmitt as the Town of Wellesley's Local Government Representative pursuant to 225 CMR 29.00, effective October 1, 2026. September 17, 2026 Dear Members of the Select Board, I’m pleased to support Tanya Auger’s reappointment to the Wellesley Cultural Council. Having served with Tanya during her first term, I have seen firsthand the thoughtful perspective, experience and commitment she brings to our work. Tanya has been an engaged and valuable member of the Council, particularly during our annual grant review process. She approaches applications carefully and thoughtfully, drawing on a background that spans education, literature, arts programming and community engagement. She understands both the importance of supporting strong cultural programs and our responsibility to make thoughtful decisions about how the Council’s limited funding is allocated. Her experience outside the Council also makes her particularly well suited to this work. Tanya serves as ESOL Program Coordinator at the Wellesley Free Library and has been involved in the Library’s strategic planning efforts. She has also spent many years working with children’s and young adult literature, including nearly 30 years reviewing books for The Horn Book, and has organized arts and author programming through the Wellesley schools. Just as importantly, Tanya brings a strong understanding of Wellesley and the different organizations, schools and residents that make up our community. That perspective is valuable as the Council continues working to broaden awareness of our grants, reach new applicants and strengthen the role of arts and culture throughout town. Tanya has already demonstrated that she is a thoughtful, dependable and committed member of the Wellesley Cultural Council. I’m very happy to support her reappointment and look forward to continuing to work with her during a second term. Thank you for your consideration. Fiscal Year begins August 18 - Updates SB on FY2026 results September 7 - HR Board reviewed COLA Recommendations September 22– SB discusses Revenues, Capital Guidelines September 29 – All Board Meeting October 5 – HR Board votes COLA October 6 - SB discusses FY 2028 Operating and Capital Budget guidelines/Individual guidelines SB discusses Non-Union COLA (Non-Exempt 1-8 and Exempt 7E-15) and MPP October 13 – SB votes FY 2028 Operating and Capital Budget guidelines October 16 – Operating budget manual & operating/capital forms distributed November 17 – Town-wide FMD Capital update to SB November 17 – Open Annual Town Meeting Warrant November 20 – Capital budget requests submitted to Finance from ALL departments November 25 – Operating budgets due from Select Board departments. December 1 – Tax Classification Hearing December 7 – School Budget is released December 8- Operating budgets due from All Non-Select Board departments. Finance begins budget compilation. December 8 - Select Board’s Budget Workshop (Day) December 8- School Budget presentation to School Committee December 16 through January 26 – School Committee, School Budget Review Continued December 22 – Warrant Closes for Annual Town Meeting January 5 - Select Board to review budget roll up, determine budget gap & begin closing process January 6 through February 24 – Advisory Review of Departmental Budgets January 26– School Committee Budget Public Hearing February 9– School Committee Votes FY28 Budget February 10 – Draft TWFP Presentation February 10 – School Committee Advisory Budget Presentation February 24 – Advisory Public Hearing for ATM March 2 - Annual Town Election March 29 - Annual Town Meeting to begin Select Board Updates Proposed Policies Drafts Available on Policy Webpage Withholding of Permits • Implements the Town’s authority to deny permits and licenses for applicants with unpaid municipal charges (with specific exceptions). • Establishes a consistent process across Town licensing authorities. • Provides notice, hearing, and payment-resolution opportunities before action is taken. Abutter Parcel Sales • Does NOT mean that all surplus Town-owned parcels are to be sold • Provides an optional process for the Select Board to sell certain small, unneeded Town-owned parcels; would apply only when the Select Board determines a parcel should be considered for disposition. • Town Meeting approval of dispositions is required. • Establishes consistent eligibility, pricing, and review standards when the program is used. School Facilities Projects Select Board Updates Debt Management and Capital Stabilization • Significant Capital Expenditure Proposed • Number, Scale and Complexity over coming 5-10 years • Board initiatives: • Capital Planning - CapCom established Feb 2026 to improve coordination, evaluation, sequencing and alignment with policies • Debt Management – consideration of policies to guide the share of debt service as a percentage of gross revenues, and the level of total outstanding debt as a percentage of Equalized Values • Debt Service Moderation – consideration of a Capital Stabilization Fund as a means to shave the peak of borrowing costs for major capital projects • Financial policy development ongoing Select Board Updates Development Projects • Mass Bay Community College – In litigation • 49 Walnut Street • Completed PSI review for construction as of right of 28 units, 6 affordable • In Wetlands Review • 888 Worcester • Acquired by Jumbo Capital for assisted/independent/memory care • Will require rezoning • 592 Washington Stret • In Site Plan Review • Recent Sales • Lower Falls: 11 Acres currently sold to Boylston Properties • Taylor Block (Wellesley Bakery/Tutto) – Sold to Jumbo Capital • 110 Cedar – Sold to Jumbo Capital • Wellesley Square – Hired Toole Design, public meetings scheduled for 10/14/26 and 11/18/26 Select Board Updates Citizen Leadership Academy (CLA) • First CLA is underway! Mr. Tobin urged the NRC, Select Board, trustees, and the WCLT to work together over the coming months to resolve outstanding questions. text: West Tisbury Zoning Board of Appeal Agenda Thursday, September 24, 2026 @ 5:00 pm In Person meeting at West Tisbury Town Hall ***Please note: all business will consist of a discussion and possible vote to take action*** 5:00 pm – Minutes of September 10, 2026, meeting. 5:15 pm – A public hearing on an APPEAL filed by Wesley Nagy of the July 31, 2026 determination made by the Building Inspector that the property located at 72 Rogers Path, Map 15, Lot 29.2, in the RU District, is in violation of Conditions 1, 4, and 5 of the Planning Board’s Special Permit dated December 26, 2024, and applicable provisions of the West Tisbury Zoning Bylaw concerning alterations to the Rogers Path Special Way and storage containers in the RU District. The appeal also challenges the corrective orders issued by the Building Inspector. The appeal is made pursuant to M.G.L. c. 40A, §§ 8 and 14. 5:45 pm – A public hearing on an application for a Special Permit from Sourati Engineering Group, LLC on behalf of Alyssa M. Halisky to allow the construction of a 12’x25’ inground swimming pool requiring 26 ft. of side yard setback relief and to allow a 6’x8’ pool shed to be located 5’ from the south property line instead of 10’ under Sections 8.5-4C and 4.2-2D4 of the West Tisbury Zoning Bylaw at 152 Vineyard Meadow Farms Rd., Map 37 Lot 33, in the RU district. Notice of Meetings Name of committee, board, etc: Planning Board Date of Meeting: Time: September 23, 2026 6:00 p.m. (Note Time) Town Hall Hearing Room 1146 Route 28, South Yarmouth, MA 02664 Place: OR Zoom Link: https://us02web.zoom.us/J/89836415124 Phone: +1 301 715 8592 and enter webinar ID: 898 3641 5124 Agenda (Topics to be discussed): 1. PUBLIC HEARING - Zoning Bylaw Amendments and General Bylaw: Draft Zoning Articles and General Bylaw related to Short-Term Rentals, and Draft Zoning Article for Accessory Dwelling Units: a. Short Term Rental Articles: i) Article 1 - General Bylaw Chapter 110 – Short Term Rentals: New General Bylaw to regulate Short-Term Rentals, which will replace the regulatory provisions currently within Zoning Bylaw Section 418, and includes Purpose, Definitions, Ineligible Units, Registration and Inspections, Limitations on Short-Term Rentals, General Provisions, Rental Listing Requirements, Penalties and Enforcement, and Severability. ii) Article 2 - Short Term Rentals: Amend Section 202.5 – Use Regulation Table to continue the A13 – Short-Term Rentals by-right use, prohibit the use in the MU and MOD zoning districts, and reference General Bylaw Chapter 110 – Short-Term Rentals in Footnote 54; and amend Section 418.6 – Sunset Clause to extend the sunset clause for Section 418 to the date when the General Bylaw Chapter 110 becomes effective, at which time Section 418 of the Zoning Bylaw would expire. This Article would be withdrawn if the General Bylaw does not pass. iii) Article 3 - Short Term Rentals: Amend Section 418.6 – Sunset Clause of the Zoning Bylaw to extend the expiration date for the Sunset Clause in Section 418 – Short-Term Rentals. This Article would be withdrawn if the other STR Articles pass. b. Article 4 - Accessory Dwelling Units: Amendments to the Accessory Apartment Zoning Bylaw to match the mandated changes from The Affordable Homes Act (Section 8 of Chapter 150 of the Acts of 2024) and current regulations 760 CMR 71.00: Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Units, while maintaining as many existing provisions as allowed by the state regulations. 2. Discussion on Executive Office of Housing & Livable Communities 2026 ADU Draft Regulations with Public Comments due October 9th 3. Discussion on Public Hearing Comments on Special Town Meeting Warrant Articles, possible changes to the Articles, and Possible Vote on Recommendations 4. Mattacheese Utilization Project (MUP): Updates on the status of the MUP project. 5. Meeting Minutes 6. Board of Appeals Agenda & Decisions 7. Committee Updates from Board Members 8. Board Member Items 9. Correspondence 10. Staff Updates 11. Other Topics not reasonably anticipated 48 hours in advance of the meeting. 12. Upcoming Meetings: a. October 6, 2026 – Meet with Select Board b. October 7, 2026 c. October 20, 2026 – Meet with Select Board – Execution of Special Town Meeting Warrant d. October 21, 2026 e. November 4, 2026 f. November 16, 2026 – Special Town Meeting 13. Article Summary: • Continues the Use of STRs within the Zoning Bylaw in accordance with the provisions in the new General Bylaw. • Extends the Sunset Clause in Zoning Bylaw Section 418 to the effective date of the General Bylaw to avoid any gaps in regulations. • This Article would be withdrawn if the General Bylaw does not pass. 3 - Short-Term Rentals (STRs) – Sunset Clause Purpose: Should the other STR Articles fail, this Article would extend the sunset clause to retain the use and the excise tax revenues while further study and evaluation is completed. Article Summary: • Extends the Sunset Clause to December 31, 2029. • This Article would be withdrawn if the other STR Articles pass. 1-3 Short-Term Rentals (STRs) Articles QUESTIONS/COMMENTS https://yarmouth.ma.us/DocumentCenter/View/21762 4 – Accessory Dwelling Units – State Mandates Purpose: Update local ADU zoning to conform with state mandates under the MA Affordable Homes Act and 760 CMR 71.00 - Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Units, while retaining as many existing provisions as possible. State Mandate: Affordable Homes Act requires all Towns to allow ADUs as of right in all zoning districts that allow single family homes. What We Can No Longer Regulate/Require:  Special Permit  Minimum Lot Size  Maximum number of bedrooms or smaller ADU sizes  Owner Occupancy  2 Parking Spaces  Ineligible units or types of developments  Requirements beyond those of a single-family home  Certain conditions from previous Accessory Apartment Special Permits 4 – Accessory Dwelling Units – State Mandates Article Summary:  One ADU per Lot  OKH design requirements apply  Minimum Unit size of 350 SF  Additions and new detached structures to meet setback/height restrictions  No parking, or expansion of parking, into green spaces in front of dwelling  Cannot be held in separate ownership (no condominium form of ownership)  ADUs can’t be STRs  No commercial uses, except Home Offices/Home Occupations per Section 416  Annual registration  Principal Dwellings on a property with an ADU can’t be used for STRs  900 SF or 50% of the GFA of the Principal Dwelling, whichever is smaller  1 parking space/ADU or none within 0.5 mile of a Transit Station • Section 6 Findings from ZBA for non-conforming structures • Mechanism to remove past restrictions through the ZBA 4 – Accessory Dwelling Units – State Mandates Article Summary (cont’d):  Includes a provision for ADUs to be someone’s Primary Residence (may not be allowed by the Attorney General as may conflict with 760 CMR and Yarmouth has not accepted Seasonal Community Designation.) More Changes Coming:  Draft revisions to 760 CMR 71.00: Protected Use Accessory Dwellings: Public comments accepted through October 9th 4 – Accessory Dwelling Units – State Mandates QUESTIONS/COMMENTS https://yarmouth.ma.us/DocumentCenter/View/21762 Zoning Amendments and General Bylaw for 2026 Special Town Meeting The Yarmouth Planning Board will hold a Public Hearing on Wednesday, September 23, 2026 at 6:00 P.M. in the Hearing Room of the Yarmouth Town Offices, 1146 Route 28, South Yarmouth, and via remote access at https://us02web.zoom.us/J/89836415124, to solicit input on four proposed Articles for the November 16, 2026 Special Town Meeting. These Articles amend the Yarmouth Zoning Bylaw related to Short-Term Rentals (STRs) and Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs); and adds a new General Bylaw to regulate ShortTerm Rentals. 1. STR Article 1 - General Bylaw Chapter 110 – Short-Term Rentals: This Article creates a new General Bylaw to regulate STRs which will replace the regulatory provisions currently located within Section 418 of the Zoning Bylaw. Through further study and public engagement, the STR regulations have been modified and fine-tuned to help reduce the commercialization of STRs, improve enforcement tools, and further address quality of life issues. STRs are an important source of revenue to the Town through increased economic activity and through STR excise taxes which brought in over $2.375 Million in FY26, 75% of which goes towards our municipal wastewater program. Some key provisions and modifications contained within the General Bylaw include: • further restrictions on types of dwellings that can be used as a STR • limiting owners to one STR in Yarmouth while grandfathering the few owners who currently have multiple STRs • further clarifications on occupancy, parking, noise, and type of rentals • identification of specific information to be included within all STR listings, and • enhanced penalties and enforcement including the potential revocation of a Rental Occupancy Certificate related to verified violations. In addition to these bylaw enhancements, other administrative procedures will be enacted for the 2027 season, such as: • an on-line STR complaint form • improved education of the regulations to STR owners, and • collection of additional information in the application process including Department of Revenue Registration number. 2. STR Article 2 – Zoning Bylaw Amendments: This Article would continue the use of Short-Term Rentals within the Zoning Bylaw in accordance with the provisions in the new General Bylaw Chapter 110 – Short-Term Rentals. To accommodate different effective dates between Zoning Bylaws and General Bylaws and avoid any gaps in regulations, the Sunset Clause in Zoning Bylaw Section 418 would be extended to the date when the new General Bylaw becomes effective, at which time Section 418 would expire. This Article would be withdrawn if the General Bylaw does not pass. 3. STR Article 3 – Zoning Bylaw Amendments - Sunset Clause: Should other Articles related to ShortTerm Rentals not pass, this Article would extend the Sunset Clause contained in Section 418 to ensure the continuation of Short-Term Rentals in Yarmouth and the excise tax revenues they bring to the Town while further study and evaluation can be completed. This Article would be withdrawn if the other ShortTerm Rental Articles pass. 4. ADU Zoning Article 1 - Accessory Apartments: This Article seeks to update local zoning regulations concerning Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) to conform with state mandates under the Massachusetts Affordable Homes Act (Chapter 150 of the Acts of 2024) amending M.G.L. c. 40A, § 3, and 760 CMR 71.00 - Protected Use Accessory Dwelling Units. The Affordable Homes Act requires all Towns in Massachusetts to allow accessory dwelling units as of right in all zoning districts that allow single family homes. Revisions are proposed to meet the state mandate while retaining as many existing provisions as allowable and include: unit sizes up to 900 sf or 50% of the principal dwelling’s gross floor area, whichever is smaller; minimum unit size of 350 sf; one ADU per lot; new construction to meet setbacks and building height requirements; outlines types of nonconformities requiring a Section 6 Finding from the Zoning Board of Appeals; prevents separate ownership of the ADU; includes adherence to the Old King’s Highway Historic District requirements; reduces parking requirements to match state regulations while preventing parking in existing green spaces in front of the building; prohibits Short-Term Rentals in an ADU or in the principal dwelling on a lot with an ADU; no commercial uses other than limited Home Offices and Home Occupations; and limits enforceability of restrictions and regulations on preexisting ADUs. Per 760 CMR 71.00, some provisions in our current zoning bylaw have been eliminated as they are no longer enforceable, such as requiring a Special Permit, owner occupancy, minimum lot size, 2 parking spaces per ADU, ineligibly properties, and any requirements for an ADU not also required for a singlefamily home. Codifying these changes to the zoning bylaw to comply with 760 CMR 71.00 provides clarity for future applicants, makes it easier to enforce, and clearly outlines the provisions we want to retain within the constraints of the state law. STR ARTICLE 1 – General Bylaw Chapter 110 – Short-Term Rentals: To see if the Town will vote to add to the Town of Yarmouth General Bylaws Chapter 110 – Short Term Rentals, or take any other action relative thereto, as follows: Chapter 110 SHORT-TERM RENTALS § 110-1. Purpose. To provide for the orderly operation of short-term rentals for residential properties that balance private, neighborhood and public interests, and will: 1. Protect and maintain the residential character of existing neighborhoods. 2. Protect public health and safety. 3. Protect and preserve year-round housing stock. 4. Inhibit the commercialization of housing for use as Short Term Rentals. 5. Enable residents to better afford to live in Yarmouth, maintain their properties and contribute to the community. 6. Ensure the continued revenues to the Town from the short-term rental excise tax. § 110-2. Definitions. OWNER – Any person, corporation, LLC, trust or other entity that, alone, or severally with others, directly or indirectly, has legal or equitable title or beneficial interest in any dwelling unit. OPERATOR – A person or entity who is designated by an Owner to be responsible for the dayto-day operations of the Short-Term Rental and who serves as the local 24-hour emergency contact person with the Town of Yarmouth. An Owner may also be an Operator provided they are available 24 hours a day during the rental period to address operational issues at the Short-Term Rental.
